description: Rhythm section layer: drum character, the kit or machine it comes from, an extra percussion element, and the bass approach.

styles.name: Crunchy
styles.note: Clip the transients slightly. Analog-style distortion.

styles.name: Dirty
styles.note: Leave the bleed and the noise in.

styles.name: Clean
styles.note: No saturation. Every hit readable.

styles.name: Punchy
styles.note: Short, fast attack, tight decay.

styles.name: Heavy
styles.note: Big low end on the kick, thick snare body.

styles.name: Soft
styles.note: Low velocity, brushed feel, nothing sharp.

styles.name: Vinyl
styles.note: Sampled off a record, hiss included.

styles.name: Compressed
styles.note: Smash the bus until it breathes with the loop.

styles.name: Loose
styles.note: Off-grid, unquantized, alive.

styles.name: Humanized
styles.note: Vary velocity and timing on every hit.

styles.name: Dusty
styles.note: Dark, filtered, sitting behind the sample.

styles.name: Tight
styles.note: Gated, short, surgically placed.

styles.name: Boomy
styles.note: Long kick tail. Let it ring into the next bar.

styles.name: Snappy
styles.note: Snare cuts through everything else.

styles.name: Saturated
styles.note: Tape or tube drive on the drum bus only.

styles.name: Muffled
styles.note: Like the drums are in the next room.

styles.name: Live Kit
styles.note: Room mics, full kit, real player energy.

styles.name: Gated
styles.note: Hard gate with a long, abrupt release.

styles.name: Distorted
styles.note: Push past clipping. Damage is the texture.

styles.name: Minimal
styles.note: Kick and snare only. Nothing else survives.

styles.name: Layered
styles.note: Three samples per hit, tuned to the same note.

styles.name: Swung
styles.note: Heavy shuffle on the hats, straight kick.

styles.name: Machine
styles.note: Rigid, robotic, zero humanization.

styles.name: Breakbeat
styles.note: One break, chopped and rearranged, no layering.

styles.name: Trap Hats
styles.note: Rolls, triplets, and velocity ramps.

styles.name: Broken
styles.note: Displace the snare. Never resolve the pattern.

styles.name: 808 Flavour
styles.note: Long sub kick, tick hats, handclap.

styles.name: 909 Flavour
styles.note: Punchy machine kick and open hat wash.

styles.name: MPC Chopped
styles.note: Pads played by hand, one take, no edits.

styles.name: Half-Time
styles.note: Snare on beat 3 only. Let it hang.

kits.name: SP-1200
kits.note: 12-bit crunch, 10 seconds of memory, all attitude.

kits.name: MPC60
kits.note: Swing at 54% and never look back.

kits.name: MPC2000XL
kits.note: The sound of a decade of basements.

kits.name: TR-808
kits.note: Tune the kick to the key of the song.

kits.name: Acoustic Kit
kits.note: Recorded in a room, mics included.

kits.name: Sampled Break
kits.note: Pull the whole kit from one 4-bar break.

kits.name: Stock DAW Kit
kits.note: Whatever came with your DAW. Make it sound expensive.

kits.name: Found Sounds
kits.note: Build the kit from non-instrument recordings.

kits.name: Hybrid Stack
kits.note: Acoustic snare, machine kick, sampled hats.

bass.name: Upright Bass
bass.note: Walking or sustained, always slightly behind.

bass.name: 808 Bass
bass.note: Glide between notes. Let it distort.

bass.name: Sampled From Loop
bass.note: Extract the bass from the sample itself.

bass.name: No Bass
bass.note: Let the sample's low end carry the whole track.

bass.name: Melodic Bass
bass.note: The bass is the hook. Write it first.

bass.name: Octave Doubled
bass.note: Sub underneath, mid-bass on top, same line.

bass.name: Drone Bass
bass.note: One note for the entire beat.
